privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.body:
Effective date 26 September 2026 Last updated 26 September 2026

1. Who we are

Ideovent Technologies is a partnership firm under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, founded in 2024, whose two partners are Mehdi Alam and Abhishek Tiwari, with its principal place of business at Saket, New Delhi, India.

For the purposes of India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 ("DPDP Act") we are the Data Fiduciary for personal data collected through www.ideovent.in. For the purposes of the EU General Data Protection Regulation and the UK GDPR ("GDPR"), where those laws apply to a visitor, we are the controller of that same data.

FieldValue
BusinessIdeovent Technologies (a partnership firm)
ConstitutionPartnership firm under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932
PartnersMehdi Alam, Abhishek Tiwari
AddressSaket, New Delhi, India
Phone / WhatsApp+91 77619 21786
Emailcontact@ideovent.in
Websitewww.ideovent.in

2. What this policy covers. And what it does not

This policy explains what happens to personal data collected through our own website, through enquiry emails and WhatsApp messages sent to us, and in the ordinary course of quoting for and delivering a project.

It does not cover personal data we handle inside a client’s own system, for example records in a school portal or an EduFlow instance we build and maintain. There, the client is the Data Fiduciary / controller and Ideovent acts as a Data Processor on the client’s documented instructions, under the signed services agreement and any data processing terms attached to it. Section 10 explains this in more detail, because it matters most where student data is involved.

3. What we collect

a. Information you give us directly

  • Contact and enquiry forms. Your name, email address, phone number, organisation name, and whatever you type into the message field.
  • Email, phone and WhatsApp: the content of your message, your contact details, and anything you attach.
  • Proposals, agreements and invoices, billing name, billing address, tax identifiers where you supply them, and the contact details of the people you nominate for the project.
  • Recruitment or collaboration enquiries: a CV or portfolio link, if you send one.

b. Information collected automatically when you visit the site

  • Server and security logs kept by our hosting provider: IP address, browser and device type operating system, referring page, pages requested, and the date and time of the request.
  • Cookies and similar technologies, see section 13. The site sets no advertising or analytics cookies.

c. What we ask you not to send us

Please do not put sensitive information into a website form or an unencrypted email, financial account details, health or biometric information, government identifiers, login credentials, or personal data about third parties such as students or patients. If your project involves data of that kind, tell us and we will set up a secure channel before anything is shared.

4. Why we use your data, and our legal basis

What we doData usedBasis under the DPDP Act (India)Basis under the GDPR (EU / UK)
Reply to an enquiry and discuss your requirementContact details, message contentConsent: the data is given voluntarily for this specified purposeSteps taken at your request before entering a contract, Art. 6(1)(b)
Prepare a proposal, scope and quotationContact and organisation details, project informationConsentPre-contractual steps, Art. 6(1)(b)
Deliver a project and support itProject contacts, access credentials you providePerformance of the engagementPerformance of a contract, Art. 6(1)(b)
Raise invoices and keep accounting recordsBilling details, payment referencesCompliance with lawLegal obligation, Art. 6(1)(c)
Keep the website available and secureServer logs, IP addressLegitimate use, security and prevention of misuseLegitimate interests, Art. 6(1)(f)
Send project updates or occasional service emailsName, email addressConsentConsent, or legitimate interests for existing clients
Establish, exercise or defend a legal claimWhatever is relevant to the disputeLegitimate useLegitimate interests, Art. 6(1)(f)

We do not sell personal data, we do not share it with data brokers, and we do not use it to build advertising profiles.

5. How long we keep it

CategoryRetentionThen
Enquiries that do not become projects24 months from the last messageDeleted
Client project records and correspondenceThe life of the engagement plus 3 yearsDeleted or anonymised
Invoices, receipts and accounting recordsFor as long as Indian income tax and GST law requires us to keep themDeleted once the statutory period expires
Website server and security logsAs kept by our host, Vercel: no more than 30 days, and as little as 1 hour on some plansOverwritten automatically
Analytics dataNone. No analytics data is collectedDeleted, or aggregated so no individual can be identified
Signed contracts and NDAsThe term plus the survival period stated in the documentArchived, then destroyed

If you ask us to erase your data earlier, we will, unless the law requires us to keep it: an invoice that must stay in the accounting records, for example.

6. Who else touches your data

We keep the list of processors short on purpose. These are the only categories of service provider that touch personal data collected through this site, who each one is, and the country it processes that data in.

CategoryWhat they doProviderWhere they process
Website hostingServes the site and keeps server logsVercel Inc. (USA)Vercel's global network. The site is static and is served from the Vercel location nearest each visitor, anywhere in the world
Contact form handlingReceives and stores form submissionsEmailJS (email delivery of the form) and Supabase (lead storage)EmailJS: USA (Amazon Web Services). Supabase: Mumbai, India. Until our Supabase database is switched on, forms are delivered by email only
Business emailSends and stores our emailGoogle (Gmail)Google data centres in several countries, including the USA
Website analyticsReports on site usageNone. The site loads no analytics or tracking scriptn/a
Payment processingCollects card, UPI or bank paymentsRazorpay (Razorpay Software Private Limited)India

Each provider is bound by its own terms and processes data on our instructions. Card numbers and bank credentials go directly to the payment gateway. Ideovent never sees or stores a full card number.

We may also disclose personal data where we are legally required to, to a court, a regulator or a law-enforcement agency acting under proper authority, or where it is necessary to establish or defend a legal claim. If the business is ever transferred, personal data may transfer with it, and we will tell the people affected before that happens.

7. Where your data is stored, and international transfers

Ideovent operates from India. What you send through this site's forms is delivered to us by email. EmailJS passes it through servers in the USA, and it is then kept in our Gmail inbox, which Google stores in data centres in several countries, including the USA. Until our Supabase database is switched on, the site also saves a copy of what you submit in your own browser’s local storage, on your device. That copy is not sent to us or anyone else, and you can remove it by clearing this site’s data in your browser. Once the database is switched on, form submissions will be stored in Mumbai, India instead of in your browser. All of it is accessible from India.

If you are in the EEA or the UK, that means your personal data is transferred outside your home jurisdiction. India is not covered by an EU or UK adequacy decision. Where a transfer takes place we rely on the Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission, and on the UK International Data Transfer Addendum for UK transfers, together with the practical safeguards in section 11. A copy of the transfer terms we rely on is available on request to contact@ideovent.in.

Whether we must appoint an EU or UK representative under Article 27 GDPR depends on the scale and regularity of our offering into those markets. Current position: no representative has been appointed. We will appoint one if the law requires it.

Under section 16 of the DPDP Act the Government of India may restrict transfers of personal data to specified countries. We will comply with any such notification.

8. Your rights

If you are in India. Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023

As a Data Principal you have the right to

  • Access: a summary of the personal data we hold about you, how it is being processed, and the identities of anyone we have shared it with.
  • Correction, completion, updating and erasure of your personal data.
  • Withdraw consent at any time, as easily as you gave it. Withdrawal does not undo processing that has already lawfully happened.
  • Grievance redressal, raise a complaint with our Grievance Officer (section 14) and get a response before approaching the Data Protection Board of India.
  • Nominate another individual to exercise these rights on your behalf if you die or become incapacitated.

You also have duties under section 15 of the Act, including not filing a false or frivolous complaint and not impersonating another person when making a request.

If you are in the EEA or the UK, GDPR / UK GDPR

You have the right to access your data, to rectification, to erasure, to restriction of processing, to data portability, to object to processing based on legitimate interests and to withdraw consent where processing rests on consent. We do not carry out automated decision-making or profiling that produces legal effects.

You may complain to your national supervisory authority, in the UK, the Information Commissioner’s Office (ico.org.uk). We would appreciate the chance to put it right first.

If you are in the United States

We are not a "business" within the meaning of the California Consumer Privacy Act as currently drafted, because we do not meet its revenue or volume thresholds. Even so we do not sell or share personal information as those terms are used in US state privacy laws, and we will honour a request to access or delete your data on the same terms as everyone else. Marketing email, if we ever send any, always carries a working unsubscribe link, as CAN-SPAM requires.

9. How to make a request

Email contact@ideovent.in with the subject line "Data request", or write to the postal address in section 1. Tell us what you want done and give us enough detail to find your records.

  • We may ask you to confirm your identity, usually by replying from the email address already in our records. We will not ask for identity documents unless there is a real doubt.
  • We respond within 30 days. If a request is unusually complex we will tell you inside those 30 days why we need longer, and how much longer. GDPR requests are answered inside one month.
  • There is no charge. If a request is repetitive or clearly excessive we will explain why we are charging a reasonable fee or declining it, and you can challenge that decision.

If our response does not satisfy you, write to the Grievance Officer in section 14. If you are still not satisfied you may complain to the Data Protection Board of India, or to your own supervisory authority if you are in the EEA or the UK.

10. Children’s and students’ data

This deserves its own section, because schools and coaching institutes are among our clients.

Our website is not directed at children. We do not knowingly collect personal data from anyone under 18 through www.ideovent.in. Our enquiry forms are meant for the adult who runs or represents an organisation. If you believe a child has submitted personal data through the site, write to contact@ideovent.in and we will delete it.

Student data inside a school system is a different matter. When we build or maintain a school portal, a coaching platform or an EduFlow instance, the student records in that system belong to the institution. The institution is the Data Fiduciary; Ideovent acts only as a Data Processor and

  • processes student data only on the institution’s written instructions, and only to build, fix migrate or support the system;
  • never uses student data for our own purposes, never sells it, and never uses it for advertising behavioural tracking or targeted advertising directed at children. Which the DPDP Act prohibits in any event;
  • accesses production data only when it is genuinely necessary, and works with anonymised or reduced test data wherever the task allows;
  • deletes or returns student data at the end of the engagement, on the institution’s instruction;
  • expects the institution to obtain verifiable consent from a parent or lawful guardian where the DPDP Act requires it for a child under 18, and to satisfy any equivalent requirement under GDPR Article 8 for an EU or UK institution. That consent is the institution’s responsibility, not ours, and we do not collect it on their behalf unless the signed agreement says so in writing.

Institutions should put these points into the services agreement or a separate data processing addendum rather than rely on a website policy. We are happy to sign one.

11. How we protect your data

We are a small firm and we describe our security honestly rather than dress it up.

  • Encryption in transit: the site is served over HTTPS/TLS, and administrative access to hosting, code and email uses encrypted connections.
  • Access control, access to systems holding personal data is limited to the partners of the firm and to any team member or contractor who needs it for a specific task, under a signed confidentiality agreement.
  • Authentication, multi-factor authentication is enabled on every account that supports it including code hosting, cloud hosting and email.
  • Minimisation. We ask for the least data that lets us do the job, and prefer masked or sample data in development environments.
  • Backups, project data is backed up, and backups sit inside the same protected accounts.
  • Vendor selection. We use established providers rather than unknown low-cost services, and we read their security terms before adopting them.

No system is perfectly secure and we do not claim otherwise. What we do undertake is not to quietly absorb a problem that affects you, see the next section.

12. If there is a personal data breach

If personal data in our control is lost, exposed or accessed without authorisation, we will

  1. contain the incident and establish exactly what data, and whose data, is affected;
  2. notify every affected person without undue delay, in plain language: what happened, what data was involved, what we are doing, and what you should do;
  3. notify the Data Protection Board of India in the form and within the time the DPDP Act and its rules require;
  4. where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies, notify the relevant supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, unless it is unlikely to result in a risk to people’s rights;
  5. where we act as a processor for a client, notify that client without undue delay so they can meet their own obligations, and support their investigation.

13. Cookies, marketing and third-party links

This site sets no advertising, marketing or analytics cookies. What it stores on your device is limited to what the site needs to work: your light/dark theme choice, a cached copy of the site’s own content so pages load quickly, a copy of any form you submit here (see section 7), and, only if you log in to the admin area, a session marker that is discarded when you close the tab. None of it is used to track you and none of it is shared with anyone. Because nothing non-essential is set, no consent banner is shown. If analytics or any other non-essential technology is ever added, a full Cookie Policy and a consent banner will be published before it goes live, not after.

We do not run an advertising list. If we ever start a newsletter it will be opt-in, every message will carry an unsubscribe link, and unsubscribing will take effect immediately.

Our site links to other websites: a client’s live site, a tool we recommend, our GitHub or Instagram profile. Those sites have their own privacy policies and we are not responsible for them.

14. Grievance Officer

Section 13 of the DPDP Act requires a named point of contact who will answer questions about personal data. For Ideovent Technologies that is the partner named below.

FieldValue
Grievance OfficerMehdi Alam, Partner
Emailcontact@ideovent.in, subject line "Grievance, personal data"
Phone+91 77619 21786
PostSaket, New Delhi, India
Response timeAcknowledgement within 7 days; substantive response within 30 days

The same person answers GDPR and UK GDPR enquiries. We have not appointed a Data Protection Officer because our processing does not meet the Article 37 threshold that requires one.

15. Changes to this policy

We update this page when our processing changes or the law does. The last updated date at the top always reflects the current version. If a change materially affects how we use personal data you have already given us, we will tell the people affected by email rather than rely on the website notice alone.

16. Governing law

This policy is governed by the laws of India. The courts at New Delhi have jurisdiction over any dispute arising from it. Nothing here removes a right you have under the mandatory law of the country you live in, including the right to complain to your own supervisory authority.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.body:
Effective date [[POLICY_EFFECTIVE_DATE]] Last updated [[POLICY_LAST_UPDATED]]

These terms govern use of the website www.ideovent.in. They are not the contract under which we build anything for you. That is a separate signed agreement. Section 6 explains the difference, and it is the section most worth reading.

1. Who these terms are between

"We", "us" and "Ideovent" mean Ideovent Technologies, a partnership firm registered under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 (registration status: [[PARTNERSHIP_REGISTRATION_STATUS]]), whose two partners are Mehdi Alam and Abhishek Tiwari, founded in 2024, with its principal place of business at Saket, New Delhi, India. "You" means anyone who visits or uses www.ideovent.in.

By using the site you accept these terms. If you do not accept them, please do not use the site.

2. What the site is for

The site describes what Ideovent does, website development, custom SaaS, mobile apps, UI/UX design backend and API work, maintenance and support, and our EduFlow school and coaching management product. It lets you read about that work and get in touch.

The site is provided free of charge. We may change, suspend or withdraw any part of it at any time including taking it offline for maintenance, without notice and without liability to you. We do not guarantee that the site will be available uninterrupted or error-free.

3. Acceptable use

You may read, print and share pages of this site for your own information or to evaluate us as a supplier. You may not

  • use the site for any unlawful, fraudulent or harmful purpose;
  • attempt to gain unauthorised access to the site, the server it runs on, or any connected system;
  • probe, scan or test the vulnerability of the site, or breach or circumvent any security measure;
  • introduce malware, or anything designed to damage or interfere with the site or its users;
  • scrape, harvest or systematically extract content or contact details from the site, whether by automated means or otherwise, including for training a machine-learning model, except with our prior written permission;
  • send us anything through the contact form that is unlawful, defamatory, obscene, infringing, or that you do not have the right to send;
  • use the contact form or our contact details to send bulk, unsolicited or automated commercial messages;
  • impersonate any person or misrepresent your association with any organisation;
  • place an excessive load on the site, including through denial-of-service activity.

We may block access and report unlawful activity to the appropriate authorities.

4. Intellectual property in the site

All content on www.ideovent.in, text, layout, design, graphics, code, the name Ideovent Technologies, the "iV" mark and the EduFlow product name, is owned by Ideovent Technologies or used under licence, and is protected by Indian and international copyright and trade mark law.

You may not copy, reproduce, republish, adapt, frame or redistribute any part of the site for commercial purposes without our prior written permission. Short quotation with attribution and a link back is fine.

Nothing on the site transfers any right in our intellectual property to you. Intellectual property in work we produce for a client is dealt with in that client’s signed agreement, not here. And in every case rights transfer only on full payment.

Any third-party names, logos or trade marks that appear on the site remain the property of their owners and are used only to identify the technology or service concerned.

5. Accuracy of information on the site

We put the site together carefully, but it is general marketing and informational material.

  • Descriptions of services, technologies, timelines and approaches are indicative, not offers or commitments.
  • Any price, package or range shown is indicative and subject to scoping. It is not a quotation and does not bind us.
  • Technical content, guidance and blog material is general information, not professional advice for your situation. Do not act on it without taking advice that takes your facts into account.
  • The site is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranty of any kind, whether express or implied, including any implied warranty of merchantability, fitness for a particular purpose accuracy, or non-infringement, to the fullest extent permitted by law.

Our separate Disclaimer page sets out further limits, including on business results, search rankings and third-party services. It forms part of these terms.

6. Contacting us does not create a contract

This matters, so it is stated plainly.

  • Submitting the contact form, sending a WhatsApp message, emailing us, or having a discovery call does not create a contract and does not oblige either of us to anything.
  • A proposal, estimate or indicative quotation is an invitation to discuss, not an offer capable of acceptance, unless it says otherwise in writing and is signed.
  • We may decline any enquiry without giving a reason. We may already be at capacity, or the work may not suit us.
  • Work is contracted only through a separate written agreement: a Service Agreement or Master Service Agreement with a Statement of Work, signed by both sides. And, where that agreement says so, only after the advance payment is received. Until that is done, nothing has been promised no capacity is reserved and no timeline has started.
  • Where a signed agreement and these website terms differ the signed agreement prevails for that engagement.
  • Nothing you send through the contact form is treated as confidential unless we have a signed non-disclosure agreement in place. Please do not send commercially sensitive material before then; ask us for an NDA instead, and we will send one.

7. Third-party links and services

The site links to third-party sites and may reference third-party services, hosting providers payment gateways, analytics tools, app stores, client websites, our GitHub and Instagram profiles.

Those links are for convenience. We do not control those sites, we do not endorse their content, and we are not responsible for them, for their availability, or for any loss arising from your dealings with them. Their terms and privacy policies apply when you use them, not ours.

8. Limitation of liability

To the fullest extent permitted by law

  • we are not liable for any indirect, incidental, special or consequential loss arising from your use of, or inability to use, the site;
  • we are not liable for loss of profit, revenue, business, goodwill, anticipated savings, data, or for business interruption, however caused;
  • we are not liable for any decision you take in reliance on general information published on the site;
  • our total liability to you in connection with the site and these terms, whether in contract, tort (including negligence), statute or otherwise, will not exceed Rs. [[SITE_LIABILITY_CAP]] in aggregate. That cap applies to the website, which is provided free of charge. It is not the liability cap for paid project work. That one lives in the signed agreement for the engagement.

Our liability for work we are engaged to perform is governed by the limitation-of-liability clause in the signed agreement for that engagement, not by this section.

Nothing in these terms excludes or limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for anything else that cannot lawfully be excluded or limited.

Ideovent Technologies is a partnership firm and not a limited liability entity. Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 the liability of its partners is unlimited, and joint and several. Nothing in this section is to be read as limiting the liability of the firm or of its partners generally: the cap above is a cap agreed with you on our contractual liability to you in connection with this website.

9. Your responsibility to us

If you use the site in breach of section 3 and that causes us loss, claims or expense, including reasonable legal costs. You agree to reimburse us for it.

10. Privacy

Personal data collected through the site is handled as described in our Privacy Policy, and cookies as described in section 13 of that policy. Both form part of these terms.

11. Changes to these terms

We may change these terms at any time by posting a revised version on this page. The last updated date at the top shows when. Your continued use of the site after a change means you accept the revised terms. Changes do not affect any signed agreement already in force.

12. General

  • No waiver. If we do not enforce a right under these terms, we do not lose it.
  • Severability. If any provision is held unenforceable, the rest stays in force.
  • No partnership. Nothing here creates a partnership, joint venture, agency or employment relationship between us.
  • Assignment. You may not assign your rights under these terms. We may assign ours if the business is transferred.
  • Entire agreement for the site. These terms, with the Privacy Policy, the Refund and Cancellation Policy and the Disclaimer, are the whole of the terms on which the site is offered.

13. Governing law and jurisdiction

These terms and any dispute arising from them or from your use of the site are governed by the laws of India. The courts at New Delhi have exclusive jurisdiction, and both parties submit to that jurisdiction.

If you are a consumer in the EEA or the UK, this clause does not remove the protection of the mandatory consumer law of the country where you live.

refund.title: Refund and Cancellation Policy
refund.body:
Effective date [[POLICY_EFFECTIVE_DATE]] Last updated [[POLICY_LAST_UPDATED]]

This policy is written to be honoured. Ideovent Technologies is a small partnership firm. Every commitment below is one a firm of this size can actually keep. Which is why there is no blanket money-back guarantee, and why the refund clock starts when the amount is agreed rather than the day you ask.

1. Why an advance is taken at all

Ideovent is a small firm with finite capacity. When a project is confirmed, calendar weeks are blocked for it and other enquiries are declined for that period. The advance pays for that reserved capacity, not only for hours worked. That is the reason it stops being refundable once work has begun.

Payment terms for a specific project are set in the signed Service Agreement and its payment schedule, typically an advance on signing, a payment at the design-and-development milestone, and a final payment before handover. Where that signed agreement and this policy differ, the signed agreement prevails. This page is the default position for anyone who has not signed one yet, and the plain-language explanation of the one they have.

2. The short version

SituationWhat happens
You cancel before work has commencedAdvance returned, less third-party costs already incurred and a [[PRE_KICKOFF_RETENTION_PERCENT]]% reservation retention
You cancel after work has commencedAdvance is not refundable. Work done is billed; anything paid beyond that is refunded
You cancel mid-milestonePro-rata: you pay for work genuinely completed in that milestone, capped at the milestone value. The balance is refunded
A completed and accepted milestoneNot refundable
Third-party costs already spent (domains, licences, hosting, stock, app-store fees)Never refundable. We have already paid them out
You go quiet for 45+ daysNot a cancellation. Clause 7 applies
Ideovent cancels or cannot deliverYou get back everything paid for work not performed
Maintenance or retainer planCancel with notice; the paid period runs out. No part-month refund, except that an annual plan is refunded for whole unused months less the annual discount

3. What "commenced" means

This is the word that decides most refund questions, so it is defined precisely rather than left to argument. Work has commenced at the earliest of these events

  1. the kick-off call or meeting has been held;
  2. a discovery document, sitemap, wireframe, project plan or written scope has been shared with you;
  3. any design or code artefact for your project has been created and shared: a first draft, a repository, a staging environment, a deployed preview;
  4. a third-party cost has been paid on your behalf, domain, licence, template, hosting, stock asset, app-store fee;
  5. [[COMMENCEMENT_GRACE_DAYS]] calendar days have passed since your advance cleared, whichever of the above has or has not happened, because the calendar slot has by then been held and other work turned away.

Paying the advance does not, by itself, mean work has commenced. If none of events 1 to 4 has happened, the slot is still only reserved, and section 4 governs. Event 5 is the backstop: once [[COMMENCEMENT_GRACE_DAYS]] days have passed, the calendar slot has been held and other work turned away, so the engagement counts as commenced whether or not anything has been produced.

4. Cancelling before work has commenced

Tell us in writing (email to contact@ideovent.in is enough) before any of the events in section 3 happens.

You get back the advance less

  • any third-party cost already incurred or irreversibly committed on your behalf, at actual cost and with proof of payment, without mark-up; and
  • a reservation retention of [[PRE_KICKOFF_RETENTION_PERCENT]]% of the advance, covering the time already spent on scoping, quoting and scheduling, and the enquiries declined for that slot.

Nothing else is deducted, and the balance is returned on the timeline in section 9.

5. Cancelling after work has commenced

The advance is not refundable once work has commenced. It is adjusted against the fee for work actually done, not kept in addition to it.

In practice, on cancellation we will

  1. stop work on the day we receive your written notice;
  2. prepare a statement of work completed, deliverables finished, work in progress with its percentage complete, hours spent on anything charged by the hour at Rs. [[HOURLY_RATE]] per hour and third-party costs paid on your behalf;
  3. set that total against everything you have paid;
  4. if you have paid more than the total, refund the difference under section 9;
  5. if you have paid less, invoice the difference, payable within [[CANCELLATION_INVOICE_DAYS]] days.

Where the signed agreement provides for a kill fee on cancellation for convenience, currently [[KILL_FEE_PERCENT]]% of the remaining unbilled value. That fee is charged as well, as agreed compensation for reserved capacity and turned-down work. It is a genuine pre-estimate of loss, not a penalty.

6. Cancelling in the middle of a milestone

Milestones are rarely cancelled on a neat boundary, so the pro-rata position is stated in advance.

  • Work completed inside the current milestone is charged pro-rata to the proportion genuinely completed, assessed against the deliverables listed for that milestone in the Statement of Work.
  • The charge for a part-completed milestone never exceeds the full value of that milestone.
  • The remaining balance held against that milestone is refunded under section 9.
  • Where percentage completion is genuinely disputed, we will show the working, commits, files drafts, staging URLs, time records. And settle at a reasonable figure rather than argue.
  • Milestones already completed and accepted, or deemed accepted under the signed agreement, are fully payable and not refundable.

7. What happens to the work produced so far

  • Everything produced up to cancellation is handed over once everything owed has been paid source files, code repository, design files, content and credentials for the assets concerned.
  • Intellectual property transfers only on full payment. Until then the work stays ours and you have no licence to use, publish or deploy it. This is the same position as in the signed agreement.
  • We hand over work in the state it is in. A part-built site is not a finished site, it is not tested or warranted, and we do not support it after handover unless you engage us to.
  • Third-party accounts bought in your name stay yours. Accounts in our name are transferred where the provider permits it; where it does not, we will say so before you buy.
  • Project files are kept for [[POST_CANCELLATION_FILE_RETENTION_MONTHS]] months after cancellation and are then deleted. Take your copy inside that window.
  • If you go quiet. A project stalled by you for more than 45 continuous days is not a cancellation. We may treat the work completed as delivered and invoice for it, and charge a restart fee of Rs. [[REMOBILISATION_FEE]] before resuming, to cover rescheduling and the cost of holding files and environments.

8. When Ideovent is the one who cancels

If we end an engagement for convenience, or cannot deliver for a reason that is ours, illness beyond a reasonable period, capacity, a technical approach that turns out not to work

  • we give 15 days’ written notice where the agreement requires it;
  • we refund every amount received for work not performed, with no retention and no kill fee;
  • we hand over all completed deliverables for which payment has been received, including source files, with the IP for them assigned to you;
  • we do not charge a restart or cancellation fee;
  • where it helps, we will brief a successor developer at no charge for a reasonable handover period.

9. Refund timeline and method

  1. Acknowledgement, within 3 working days of your written cancellation.
  2. Statement of account: the calculation under section 5 or 6, sent within [[REFUND_STATEMENT_DAYS]] working days of acknowledgement.
  3. Agreement on the amount, by email. If you dispute the figure, tell us within 7 days and we will work through it with the evidence.
  4. Payment: any refund due is paid within [[REFUND_PROCESSING_DAYS]] working days of the amount being agreed, by the same method and to the same account the original payment came from. Bank or gateway processing time is on top and is outside our control.
  5. Deductions, payment-gateway charges on the original transaction are not recoverable by us and are deducted from the refund, as are bank charges on an international transfer, at actual cost.

International payments are refunded in the currency of the original payment. Exchange-rate movement between the payment and the refund is not to our account and is not compensated.

GST not applicable. Supplier is not registered under GST. No tax component is charged and none is refunded.

10. What is never refundable

  • Third-party costs already paid on your behalf.
  • Completed and accepted deliverables and milestones.
  • Time spent on consultation, audit, strategy or advisory sessions that have been delivered.
  • Work rejected for a reason outside the agreed scope: a change of mind about a direction already approved in writing is a change request, charged at Rs. [[HOURLY_RATE]] per hour, not a refund.
  • Amounts attributable to delay or non-delivery caused by you, content not supplied, approvals not given, access not provided.
  • Results. We do not guarantee revenue, leads, search rankings or any other business outcome, so no refund arises from an outcome not achieved. See the Disclaimer.

11. Maintenance, care plans and subscriptions

  • Billed in advance for the period stated in your plan.
  • Cancel at any time with [[SUBSCRIPTION_NOTICE_DAYS]] days’ written notice, counted from the day we receive it in writing.
  • Monthly and quarterly plans. The plan runs to the end of the period already paid for and then stops. There is no part-period refund. That period has already been reserved and staffed.
  • Annual plans paid up front: the one exception. We refund the whole calendar months left after the notice period ends, less the discount you were given for paying annually. In plain terms: the months you actually used are re-priced at the ordinary monthly rate, and the remainder comes back. Part-months are not refunded.
  • Unused hours in a period do not carry forward unless the plan says they do.

12. If something has gone wrong

Before cancelling, tell us. Most problems are fixable, and we would rather fix them.

Write to contact@ideovent.in or call +91 77619 21786 with what is wrong and what you want done about it. We will reply within 3 working days with a plan and a date. If work is genuinely defective against the agreed scope, we fix it at our own cost within the warranty period in the signed agreement. That is a rectification obligation, and it comes before any question of a refund.

13. Chargebacks

Please raise a dispute with us before raising one with your bank or card issuer. A chargeback filed while we are still in the process above is treated as a breach of the payment terms, and we may suspend work and recover the disputed amount together with any gateway penalty.

14. Governing law

This policy is governed by the laws of India, and the courts at New Delhi have jurisdiction. For international clients, the governing law and forum in the signed Master Service Agreement apply instead, where they differ.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

This page sets out what Ideovent does not promise. It is short on purpose, and it is the page to point at when an expectation was never actually agreed. It forms part of the Terms of Service and applies alongside the signed agreement for any engagement.

1. General information only

Everything published on www.ideovent.in, service descriptions, technical writing, guides comparisons and examples, is general information. It is not professional, legal, financial or technical advice for your particular situation, and it is not a recommendation to adopt any particular technology.

We write carefully and correct mistakes when we find them, but we do not warrant that the content is complete, current or free of error. Do not act on it without advice that takes your own facts into account. Any decision you take on the basis of this site is your own.

2. No guaranteed business results

We do not guarantee any business outcome. Building good software is one input into a business and it is not the only one.

Specifically, nothing said on this site, in a proposal, in a call, or in any informal message is a promise of

  • a number of leads, enquiries, bookings, admissions or sign-ups;
  • an amount of revenue, profit or cost saving;
  • a conversion rate, a bounce rate or any other performance metric;
  • growth in audience, followers or repeat customers;
  • adoption of a system by your staff, students or customers.

Results depend on your market, your pricing, your offer, your competitors, your staff, your own marketing spend, seasonality and the effort you put in after delivery. None of these is within our control. Any figure, benchmark or "typical" outcome mentioned in a conversation is context for the discussion, not a forecast and not a commitment. Where we set out what a system is designed to achieve, that is a design intent, not a guaranteed result.

What we do commit to is stated in the signed agreement: the agreed scope, built to the agreed specification, delivered on the agreed schedule, fixed at our cost if it is defective within the warranty period. That is a workmanship obligation, and it is one we stand behind.

3. No guaranteed search rankings

Search engines are third parties whose ranking systems are private, constantly changed, and outside anyone’s control. Nobody can guarantee a position on Google, and we do not.

  • We build sites on sound technical foundations, clean semantic markup, fast load times, mobile responsiveness, crawlable structure, sitemaps, metadata, structured data where relevant.
  • That is technical SEO groundwork. It improves the odds. It does not buy a ranking.
  • We do not guarantee a position, a keyword, an impression volume, click-through rate or indexing timeline for any page.
  • Rankings move with algorithm updates, competitor activity, your domain history, your content cadence and your backlinks. An update can change results overnight with no change on your site.
  • Where SEO work is in scope, it is written into the Statement of Work as activities delivered never as positions achieved.
  • Anyone promising you a guaranteed number-one ranking is either guessing or using techniques that will eventually cost you your visibility.

Similar limits apply to app-store rankings, social-platform reach and email deliverability: all governed by third-party systems we do not control.

4. Third-party services and dependencies

Modern software is assembled from services other people run. A typical project depends on some combination of hosting, DNS and domain registrars, cloud infrastructure, payment gateways, email and SMS providers, authentication providers, maps, analytics, SDKs, open-source libraries, app stores and browser platforms.

We choose these carefully, but we do not control them and we cannot be responsible for them. We accept no liability for

  • downtime, outage, degraded performance or data loss at a third-party provider;
  • a provider changing its API, pricing, terms or free tier, or discontinuing a product;
  • a provider suspending or terminating your account, or rejecting your app from a store;
  • a payment gateway declining, delaying or reversing a transaction;
  • a security incident originating with a third party;
  • a third-party licence whose terms change after we build on it.

Costs. Third-party fees, hosting, domains, licences, gateway charges, store fees, paid APIs are yours, are additional to our fee, and can change without notice. Where we buy on your behalf we charge them at actual cost with proof of payment and no mark-up, payable in advance.

Where a provider’s failure breaks something we built, we will help diagnose it and work around it where that is possible, under the support terms you hold. That is assistance, not liability.

5. Technology changes

Software does not stand still, and a system delivered today sits in an environment that will keep moving underneath it.

  • Browsers, operating systems and mobile platforms update, and can deprecate behaviour a working feature relies on.
  • Frameworks and libraries release breaking versions, and older versions eventually stop receiving security patches.
  • Security vulnerabilities are discovered in dependencies that were sound when the project shipped.
  • Laws and platform policies change, and can require changes to a compliant site.
  • Integrations break when the service at the other end changes.

A delivered system is built against the platforms, versions and browser support agreed at the time of delivery, and is warranted against that baseline. Keeping it current over time is maintenance work, not warranty work. It is covered by a care plan or charged as separate work, and we will always tell you which applies before doing it. Running an unmaintained system is a choice with consequences; we will say so, in writing, before it becomes a problem.

6. Examples, previews and demonstrations

Screenshots, demos, staging previews and sample data shown during a project illustrate an approach or a work in progress. They are not a warranty of the finished product, which is defined by the agreed scope and specification. Placeholder text and sample data exist to show structure; they are replaced with your real content before launch.

7. Estimates and timelines

Estimates are estimates. A timeline is based on the information available when it is given and on your inputs arriving when agreed, content, approvals, access, third-party accounts. Late inputs move the date. Where a firm date matters to you, say so early and we will write it into the Statement of Work with the conditions it depends on.

8. Availability of the website

We do not warrant that www.ideovent.in will be available without interruption or free of error. The site may be taken offline for maintenance at any time. Use of the site is at your own risk, and we are not liable for any loss arising from it.

9. Limitation of liability

Our liability for use of this website is limited as set out in section 8 of the Terms of Service. Our liability for work we are engaged to perform is governed by the limitation-of-liability clause in the signed agreement for that engagement.

Nothing on this page excludes or limits liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for anything else that cannot lawfully be excluded.

10. Governing law

This disclaimer is governed by the laws of India, and the courts at New Delhi have jurisdiction.
